pr.title: Skip coroutines in jump threading to avoid query cycles
pr.author: tmiasko

issues.title: Recent optimization broke async recursion in release mode
issues.body:
This code compiles in debug mode, but fails in release mode ([playground link](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=nightly&mode=release&edition=2021&gist=9d20e30784e618a34a18191fbfabc4e3)): ```rust use std::{future::Future, pin::Pin}; pub async fn foo(count: u32) { if count == 0 { return } else { let fut: Pin>> = Box::pin(foo(count - 1)); fut.await; } } ``` On release mode, it errors with: ``` Compiling playground v0.0.1 (/playground) error[E0733]: recursion in an async fn requires boxing --> src/lib.rs:3:1 | 3 | pub async fn foo(count: u32) { | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ | = note: a recursive `async fn` call must introduce indirection such as `Box::pin` to avoid an infinitely sized future For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0733`. error: could not compile `playground` (lib) due to 1 previous error ``` I bisected it down to this patch causing the issue: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/e132cac3c45217f5f2b730ddd684fdd4700ffc4c. cc @cjgillot. ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` 1.78.0-nightly (2024-02-13 a84bb95a1f65bfe25038) ```
Backtrace

``` Compiling version_check v0.9.4 Compiling typenum v1.17.0 Compiling cfg-if v1.0.0 Compiling cpufeatures v0.2.12 Compiling generic-array v0.14.7 Compiling inout v0.1.3 Compiling crypto-common v0.1.6 Compiling cipher v0.4.4 Compiling aes v0.8.4 Compiling foo v0.1.0 (/usr/local/google/home/etryzelaar/foo) error[E0733]: recursion in an async fn requires boxing --> src/lib.rs:1:1 | 1 | async fn foo(count: u32) { | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ | = note: a recursive `async fn` call must introduce indirection such as `Box::pin` to avoid an infinitely sized future ```

processing.reason: This PR fixes a compile-time query cycle (spurious E0733) caused by running JumpThreading on coroutine bodies; it is not a value-level MIR rewrite. JumpThreading's actual transformation was unchanged—the fix only adds an early `if tcx.is_coroutine(def_id) { return; }` to restrict the pass's application domain. There is no concrete input for which both the "original" and "corrected" Rust functions compile, run under Miri, and return different numeric/boolean/character values: the historical defect manifests as a compiler error (E0733 / query cycle) on a recursively boxed async fn at `-O`, not as a wrong runtime result. Encoding a differing runtime value would require inventing an unrelated jump-threading rewrite, which the PR explicitly does not change, or simulating compiler query-cycle behavior via version checks/external state, both forbidden by the task. The regression test (`tests/ui/mir/mir_query_cycle.rs`) is build-pass only and confirms no execution semantics differ. Therefore no source-grounded counterexample pair can be validated.

analysis.originalLogic: The `JumpThreading` MIR pass optimized every body it was given: it obtained `def_id` from `body.source.def_id()`, then proceeded with `let param_env = tcx.param_env_reveal_all_normalized(def_id);` and constructed the jump-threading map and loop headers with no check on the body kind.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Running jump threading on coroutine bodies caused query cycles. The historical code did not skip coroutines, so "Optimizing coroutines creates query cycles." The fix inserts `if tcx.is_coroutine(def_id) {` with a trace and `return;` before constructing the jump-threading `Map`. This is a confirmed bug fix, not a wrong jump-thread rewrite: the transformation itself was not changed, but its application domain was incorrectly too broad.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies of Rust functions compiled with optimization enabled, specifically async fns lowered to coroutines. The regression input is a recursive async fn with required indirection, e.g. `pub async fn foo(count: u32)` that returns on `count == 0` and otherwise does `let fut: Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()>>> = Box::pin(foo(count - 1));` followed by `fut.await`, compiled with `-O --crate-type=lib`, edition 2021.
analysis.summary: JumpThreading must not run on coroutine bodies because optimizing coroutines creates query cycles; recursively boxed async fns compiled with -O could fail with a spurious E0733 "recursion in an async fn requires boxing". The fix is an early `tcx.is_coroutine(def_id)` skip, with a build-pass regression test.
analysis.trigger: JumpThreading processes a coroutine MIR body, as happens for an async fn under optimized compilation such as `-O` / release mode.
preconditions: The crate is compiled with optimization (`-O`), so MIR optimization passes including JumpThreading run.
The body being optimized is a coroutine generated from an async fn.
The async fn is recursive and uses indirection such as `Box::pin` to satisfy the recursion requirement.
pitfalls: Do not describe this as a wrong control-flow rewrite; the historical defect is applying JumpThreading to coroutine bodies, which creates query cycles.

Do not claim the query cycle is visible only as a compiler crash: the linked issue reports `error[E0733]: recursion in an async fn requires boxing` in release mode while the same code compiles in debug mode.
Distinguish optimization level from the transformation: the skip belongs at JumpThreading entry before any `Map` construction or loop-header analysis.
Do not invent a replacement jump-threading rewrite for this bug; the correction is exclusively the coroutine early return.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI build-pass regression test under `tests/ui/mir/` modeled on `mir_query_cycle.rs`: build-pass, `-O --crate-type=lib`, edition 2021, containing a recursive async fn whose recursive call is boxed (`Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()>>>` via `Box::pin`). A negative/differential variant should disable or avoid the coroutine skip and demonstrate the release-mode E0733 failure, while the corrected compiler accepts the same program. Do not claim execution in this knowledge record.
